sourceCopy.name: PDF Accessibility Checker
sourceCopy.title: PDF Accessibility Checker Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Check a PDF for basic accessibility signals: tags, title, language, selectable text, figures without alt text, and heading order.
sourceCopy.intro: Inspect a PDF locally for a few machine-detectable accessibility signals, including document tags, metadata, selectable text, figures without alternate text, and heading-level jumps. This is only a first-pass checker, not a PDF/UA validator or a substitute for assistive-technology testing.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: What can this PDF accessibility checker detect?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: It reports whether the PDF exposes structure tags, a document title and language, selectable text on each page, figures with alternative text, and possible jumps in heading levels. It cannot decide if reading order or alternative text is meaningful.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Is my PDF uploaded for checking?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The selected PDF is inspected in this browser tab. The file and its text are not uploaded, saved automatically, or sent to a server.

fields.fileHint: Maximum 25 MiB and 300 pages. Inspection may use device memory; a computer is recommended for large files.
fields.title: Document title
fields.tagged: Tagged structure found on every page
fields.text: Selectable text found on every page
fields.scopeNote: These checks are heuristic. They cannot confirm correct reading order, meaningful descriptions, color contrast, keyboard use, form labels, table-header relationships, or PDF/UA/Section 508/WCAG conformance. Review manually and test with assistive technology.
fields.manualTitle: What still needs a person to review
fields.manualOrder: Check the reading order with a screen reader or PDF reading-order tool.
fields.manualAlt: Confirm every alternative description communicates the image purpose in context.
fields.manualContrast: Check color contrast, link meaning, keyboard operation, form labels, table headers, and document language.
fields.privacyNote: Inspection runs on your device after you choose a file. No upload, account, API, automatic save, or server processing.

messages.success: The first-pass report is ready. Review the limitations below.
messages.invalid: This file could not be read as a PDF. Try another file.
messages.tooLarge: The PDF is over the local limit of 25 MiB or 300 pages.
messages.textLimit: This PDF contains more than 2,000,000 extracted text characters; inspection stopped to protect device memory.
messages.failed: The PDF could not be inspected in this browser.
messages.copyUnavailable: Clipboard access is unavailable. Select the report text to copy it.

additionalFaqs.question: Does a positive result mean the PDF is accessible?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. These are limited automated signals only. A tagged PDF can still have incorrect reading order, poor descriptions, inaccessible forms, low contrast, or other barriers. Manual and assistive-technology testing is still needed.

additionalFaqs.question: Can it confirm PDF/UA or WCAG compliance?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This first-pass checker does not test every requirement and cannot certify PDF/UA, WCAG, Section 508, or legal compliance.
